coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel E4
record.summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for a roughly 90,000 sq ft arts facility (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel; E4 is in any case excluded from the developer's option). The block has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address); this hand-traced block overlaps mostly active lot 4052011 (about 77%) and 4052010 (about 15%) in that layer, which is only an overlay of approximate geometry, not an identification, and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008. No source read describes the block's current ground condition. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. E4 lies within the 28-Acre Site, whose developer is Brookfield's affiliate FC Pier 70, LLC (Port Items 9B and 12B), and DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows most of the site's re-mapped lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07) with no street address. The earlier statement that the site has not been subdivided per the masterplan's named parcels is withdrawn (named parcels have lots: Port Item 12B gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008); this block's own lot has not been identified, so this file uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's land-use designation for E4 is Retail, Arts and Light Industrial (Figure 2.1.1), with office uses permitted in Building 12 and E4 except on the ground floor, and residential not permitted on E4 (Table 2.1.1) -- not residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) calls it 'the arts building parcel (Parcel E4)' and lists it among the parcels excluded from the developer's standard option under the DDA. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. Port Item 11A (2026) proposes to allow residential use on E4 if an arts facility proves infeasible. No construction-start source found.

Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 349; option parcels are ground-leased for 99 years except condominium parcels, which may be sold)
SITELAB urban studio (lead author); Grimshaw Architecture (commercial), David Baker Architects (residential), James Corner Field Operations (landscape)
Arts (the D4D permits office uses in E4 except on the ground floor; Priority Retail required on at least 33% of its east and south frontages, S2.2.3)
50 (D4D Figure 6.4.2), the lowest of any new parcel
90,000 sq ft arts facility with replacement studio space (Port project page); 'waterfront arts facility' in the 2018 groundbreaking release
50 years at $1/year base rent with a 15-year extension option, per the 2017 DDA major terms (the memo's mark-up also shows '66 year lease')
Excluded from the developer's option under the DDA, with the affordable parcels, C1A and historic Buildings 12 and 21
Phase 2C with E1 and Building 21 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, Exhibit A)
Permanent replacement space for the Noonan Building artists 'will likely be located on the site of Parcel E4', at restricted rents tied to the Port's parameter rent (then $1.30/gsf)

The map notes now give the D4D's designation (retail, arts and light industrial, with upper-floor office allowed) instead of 'Arts only', cite Port Item 12B for the 'arts building parcel' wording, drop an uncited brochure and a generic ground-condition list, and no longer claim the site was never subdivided by the Assessor. The Item 11A milestones are dated to the Aug 7, 2026 staff report, and image credits and licence notes no longer say 'adopted' where the source doesn't. The D4D source no longer calls itself an 'adopted' document, and the Mayor's signing entry now states the Board of Supervisors' first-reading vote on Oct 31, 2017 and final passage on Nov 14, 2017.

open_questions: No arts operator, fundraising progress toward the $17.5 million, or design for the Arts Building was found; the DDA ties its start to three years after completion of the office building on Parcel 'B-2'.
SF YIMBY's 2021 summary attributes ~115,000 gsf of retail and arts space to Building 21 and ~120,000 gsf to 'E-1A and E-1B', with no separate arts building; the underlying filing was not retrieved.
Whether the Noonan Building has been demolished or its tenants relocated to temporary space: the June 2025 Port deck still lists 'Noonan Open Studios' and the Noonan Artists as active on site.
